title: test-0125-SCI-PHY-HEAT
passage: Heat is a form of energy that flows from a warmer object to a cooler one, while temperature is simply a measure of how hot or cold an object is. When you touch a metal spoon left in a hot cup of tea, it feels hot because heat energy transfers through the metal via conduction. In this process, the atoms in the metal vibrate faster and pass this energy to their neighbors without the atoms themselves moving along the spoon. If you wear a woolen sweater in winter, it does not generate its own heat. Instead, the wool acts as an insulator, trapping the air near your body to prevent your internal heat from escaping into the surroundings. Similarly, when you place a thermometer in a liquid to measure its temperature, you must keep the bulb fully submerged in the liquid while taking the reading. If you remove the thermometer, the temperature reading will change immediately because the bulb loses or gains heat from the surrounding air. Finally, heat can travel through the vacuum of space as radiation, which does not require any particles to move. This is how the sun's energy reaches the Earth, warming our planet even though space is empty.
summary: Heat flows from a warmer object to a cooler one, and temperature is just how hot or cold an object is. When you touch a metal spoon left in a hot cup of tea, it feels hot because heat energy transfers through the metal via conduction.
